slices.label: Black Southerners

runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1948 comes out as it did: Truman wins, 303–189–39. The closest state was Ohio, which went to Truman by 0.2 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1940 and 1950 census counts interpolated to 1948 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1948 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

everyone.summary: 45.9 million more adults vote. Connecticut, Louisiana, New York, Ohio flip, but Truman still wins, 343–159–29. The closest call is Illinois, which holds for Truman by 1.0 points. Dewey wins in 3 of 100 draws.
assumptions: Every adult votes. Non-citizens choose like naturalized citizens of their state and sex; Black Southerners like Black voters outside the South; everyone else as their group did in 1948.
howIGotThis: What changed: Every adult can vote, and turns out.
New voters borrow the behaviour of naturalized citizens of the same state and sex; Black voters outside the South.
The numbers: the 1940 and 1950 census counts interpolated to 1948 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1948 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

women.name: Ruth Robinson
women.quote: The President's been good to working people. We need someone who'll keep prices fair and stand up for the little fellow, not go back to the old ways.
women.controlQuote: The President's been good to working people. We need someone who'll keep prices fair and stand up for the little fellow, not go back to the old ways.

south-white.name: Anna Reed
south-white.quote: I worry about these high prices, but I can't abide the way the South-rights people carry on. The President's man seems more reasonable about keeping things moving.
south-white.controlQuote: I worry about these high prices, but I can't abide the way the South-rights people carry on. The President's man seems more reasonable about keeping things moving.

men.name: Ernest Reed
men.quote: The Republicans passed that Taft-Hartley thing to break us, and Truman says he'll undo it. That's worth my vote tomorrow, and the prices need coming down too.
men.controlQuote: The Republicans passed that Taft-Hartley thing to break us, and Truman says he'll undo it. That's worth my vote tomorrow, and the prices need coming down too.
